- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot true values, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates after strong upward moves, then underestimates as prices stabilize.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) show underestimation, suggesting model fails to capture sustained upward momentum.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price increases — lagged response to recent spikes.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) but become more accurate later (5–10 days) — suggests model needs calibration for near-term volatility.
- When history shows strong upward trend, model tends to overreact with a sharp peak, then corrects too late — implies need for dampening after spikes.
- Model underestimates true price when recent history is stable or slightly declining — fails to account for momentum carryover.
